newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen up on rescue fund, Fed rates.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen up on rescue fund, Fed rates.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to rise on Wednesday on improved sentiment following the announcement of a market support fund and on a U.S. Federal Reserve decision not to change rates, brokers said.

"The market support fund plus a decision by the U.S. Fed to leave interest rates unchanged are considered good news for the market and would induce investors to enter the market," said Witawus Charuchandr of Ekachart Finance.
The composite SET index advanced 15.91 points to 577.10 on 4.09 billion baht turnover on Monday. The market was closed on Tuesday for a Buddhist holiday.
Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said over the weekend that Thai commercial banks would pool a 50 billion baht support fund to help shore up the market.

His announcement came after the SET index fell to an eight-year low last week on market jitters following a series of negative news including speculaive attacks on the Thai baht by foreign exchange dealers.
Other measures to add liquidity to the market were expected to be announced on Wednesday and later this week.
